Subject: Question on ephemeral policy: can we have a 30-day hot+90-day cold window?

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the security questionnaire and the SOW, Legal at HealthSync is asking whether Redwood can support a hybrid retention model:

- "Hot" residency (full KV/cache/affinity) for 30 days after ingestion for realtime features;
- "Cold" short-term archive (searchable, subject to deletion API) for up to 90 days;
- After 120 days total, automatic irreversible deletion from customer-managed blobs and Redwood ephemeral layers.

Can you confirm whether that mapping is feasible and how it would appear in the Order Form/SLA (timeouts, verification, and deletion certification)? Also: are there options for expedited purge (e.g., 48-hour cert) for regulated workflows?

Appreciate a short write-up we can attach to Legal.

Best,
Tom
Tom Alvarez
Director, Product & Integrations
HealthSync

Hi Tom — thanks for outlining the ask. Putting Markus (Technical PM, Order Forms) and Priyom (Security/Product) on thread so we can give a concise response for Legal.

Short answer: yes, Redwood can support a two-tier residency with a fixed total lifecycle and an accelerated purge path; below is the operational framing we typically include in bespoke order forms. Happy to convert to Legal-friendly language.

Proposed Order Form clauses (high level):
- Residency windows: Hot (full inference residency) = 30 days after ingest. Cold (searchable archive + restricted inference) = subsequent 90 days. Total retention = 120 days.
- Deletion triggers:
  - Automated lifecycle: at day 121 the system marks data for deletion and initiates irreversible deletion from ephemeral runtime caches and customer-dedicated ephemeral storage.
  - Expedited purge: Customer may request expedited deletion; Redwood will certify completion within 48–72 hours for data stored on Redwood-managed systems, subject to in-flight inference and audit hold exceptions.
- Certification: Redwood will provide a deletion certificate (signed) and manifest listing affected resources and timestamps.
- Exceptions & Holds: For forensic/legal holds initiated by the customer, data will remain in controlled escrow for the hold period; deletion will resume after hold release.

We can also offer an optional 7-day grace snapshot if HealthSync needs a short recoverability window before irreversible deletion. Willing to put all of this into an SLA amendment + order form.

Markus / Priyom — can you add any operational or security caveats (KV cache TTLs, backup retention, encryption-at-rest/keys) that Legal will want spelled out?

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick tech addendum from my side.

Operational notes to include in Order Form and runbook:
- Hot residency: Redis/KV and inference-affine layers retained for 30 days. Continuous batching and KV population may create transient replicas; those are cleaned within the hot TTL window.
- Cold residency: Cold archive kept in deduplicated object store with restricted access keys and read-only query API for up to 90 days following hot period. Cold storage is indexable for search but inference against cold objects requires explicit warmed requests; cold inference will incur higher latency and will be subject to model/routing fallback rules.
- Deletion process:
  1) At T+121 the orchestration service submits deletion requests to ephemeral stores and object store lifecycle manager.
  2) Deletion includes KV purge, object delete, and a metadata tombstone.
  3) For S3-like object stores, Redwood triggers object delete markers and verifies eventual consistency; certification includes a job-run log and checksum-based manifest.
- Expedited purge: we can commit to a 48–72 hour SLA for purge completion for Redwood-managed subsystems. For data stored in HealthSync-managed buckets, Redwood will coordinate and provide verification artifacts but cannot enforce physical deletion timelines.
- Backups & snapshots: Redwood does not keep cross-region backups of ephemeral customer data beyond the agreed snapshot window. Any backup retention must be explicitly contracted.

I'll draft a short technical appendix and attach to the order form.

—Markus
Technical PM, Redwood Inference

Looping in the security caveats — hi Tom.

Two important security items for Legal:
1) Key custody: Redwood can support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key). If BYOK is selected we will include key-rotation windows and do not hold plaintext keys. Deletion certification will reference the key IDs used for encryption-at-rest.
2) Audit & verification: The deletion certificate will include job run-ids, timestamps, and the hash manifest for objects deleted. For compliance audits we can provide a time-limited access bundle to the audit logs.

Note on expedited purge: 48–72 hour SLA is for Redwood-managed systems only. If HealthSync keeps a copy in their own buckets (outside Redwood tenancy), Redwood will supply the same manifests and signatures but cannot execute a physical wipe. Suggest we add a clause requiring HealthSync to confirm whether any customer-managed copies exist at sign (so we can exclude them from Redwood's deletion certification).

I'll attach a 1-page technical appendix and the draft Order Form. Grace — can you circulate the order form as an amendment (one-liner billing: no charge for bespoke retention beyond base committed capacity) or do you want procurement to price it?

Cheers,
Priyom
Security & Product
Redwood Inference
